_comment: Round 3 i18n English translation drafts (coordinator review needed). Map: term-id → {enShortDesc, enLongDesc (optional)}. Generated by data team for L1 + L3 (priority layers per next_hypothesis.md). 69 terms total.

vibe-coding.enShortDesc: Term coined by Karpathy: describe intent in natural language, let LLM generate code, 'forget the code even exists'.
vibe-coding.enLongDesc:
Vibe coding is a development style coined by Andrej Karpathy in February 2025 where you fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists.

The user describes intent in natural language, the LLM generates the source, and the human mostly just vibes with the result. Best for prototypes and throwaway tools.

agentic-programming.enShortDesc: Coined by Martin Fowler: use LLM to write all code but still review code and care about internal structure. The opposite of vibe coding.
agentic-programming.enLongDesc: Agentic programming sits between vibe coding and traditional engineering. The developer uses an AI agent to produce code, but maintains professional responsibility: reviews every diff, runs tests, ensures the code is maintainable.

vibe-engineering.enShortDesc: Term coined by Simon Willison (Oct 2025): the opposite of vibe coding, for professionals who use LLMs daily.
vibe-engineering.enLongDesc:
Vibe engineering: the counter-concept to vibe coding. A vibe engineer uses AI heavily but still applies engineering discipline — code review, testing, architecture decisions.

Coined by Simon Willison in October 2025 to describe serious developers who happen to use LLMs daily.

agentic-engineering.enShortDesc: Term coined by Karpathy (Feb 2026): the mature form of vibe coding, 'more like engineering'.
agentic-engineering.enLongDesc:
Agentic engineering: Karpathy's Feb 2026 replacement for vibe coding. The mature form where you engineer the agent loop itself: spec, plans, subagents, verification, deployment.

Where vibe coding is 'forgetting code exists', agentic engineering is treating AI agents as first-class engineering artifacts.

ai-assisted.enShortDesc: Broad umbrella term for any software development that uses AI assistance, including vibe coding and agentic programming.
ai-assisted.enLongDesc:
AI-assisted software development is the umbrella term covering all use of AI in programming — autocomplete, chat, agents, and everything in between.

Subsumes: vibe coding, agentic programming, prompt-driven development, AI pair programming.

pdd.enShortDesc: Prompt-Driven Development: where the prompt is the primary driver. Karpathy called English 'the hottest new programming language'.
pdd.enLongDesc:
Prompt-Driven Development treats the natural language prompt as the source of truth, and code as a generated artifact.

Karpathy (2025): 'The hottest new programming language is English.'

pair-programming.enShortDesc: AI as a pair programming partner, collaborating with human developers. The earliest paradigm (Copilot 2021).
pair-programming.enLongDesc:
AI pair programming: the original paradigm where AI suggests code and the human accepts, rejects, or edits. Started with GitHub Copilot in 2021.

The human stays in the driver's seat; AI is the navigator.

software-for-one.enShortDesc: Kevin Roose's concept: software written for only one user (yourself), not for public use. The vibe coding era's natural output.
software-for-one.enLongDesc: Software for one: applications you build only for yourself, not for distribution. Vibe coding is the perfect paradigm because no one else needs to maintain it.

cognitive-debt.enShortDesc: Coined by Andrew Hunt (2026): the accumulated cost of AI interaction — context loss, unreliable agent behavior — beyond technical debt.
cognitive-debt.enLongDesc:
Cognitive debt: the hidden cost of AI-assisted development. The team's understanding of the codebase lags behind the code itself. AI produces code that works but nobody fully understands.

Coined by Andrew Hunt in 2026 as the next dominant engineering burden.

emotioneering.enShortDesc: Shimmin's satirical counter-term: mocking vibe coding as 'emotion engineering' rather than software engineering.
emotioneering.enLongDesc:
Emotioneering: a satirical term used by Mario Zechner and others to critique vibe coding as feeling-driven rather than discipline-driven.

Not a serious technical term, but reflects valid concerns about code quality in AI-generated output.

orchestration-of-agents.enShortDesc: The new developer role in the agentic engineering era: from writing code to managing AI agents.
orchestration-of-agents.enLongDesc:
Orchestration of AI agents: the meta-skill of designing how multiple agents collaborate, what they delegate, and how they verify each other's work.

Tools: LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen.

multi-agent-parallelism.enShortDesc: Multiple AI agents working in parallel on different problems. Shimmin used this to write a complete Rust compiler in a week.
multi-agent-parallelism.enLongDesc:
Multi-agent parallelism: spinning up multiple agents to solve sub-problems in parallel, then merging results.

Trade-off: 10x speed, but harder verification and context merging.

agentic-workflow.enShortDesc: Agarwal's term: multi-step agent execution flows. Without engineering practices, they produce technical debt at machine speed.
agentic-workflow.enLongDesc: Agentic workflow: a multi-step pipeline where AI agents plan, act, observe, and iterate. Without guardrails, these flows generate tech debt faster than humans can review.

cognitive-debt-vs-tech-debt.enShortDesc: Hunt's framework: 2025 was the year of technical debt, 2026 transitions to cognitive debt. The type of engineering burden is shifting.
cognitive-debt-vs-tech-debt.enLongDesc:
Cognitive debt vs technical debt: the migration from 'code we don't understand' to 'code we don't even remember why we wrote'.

Both require discipline; cognitive debt is harder to measure.

no-code.enShortDesc: Adjacent paradigm to vibe coding: build applications via visual drag-and-drop instead of code.
no-code.enLongDesc:
No-code platforms: tools like Webflow, Bubble, Lovable that let non-developers build applications without writing code.

Overlaps with vibe coding in the 'for non-engineers' use case, but no-code tools have stricter UI constraints.

machine-speed.enShortDesc: The speed at which AI agents produce technical debt — orders of magnitude faster than humans. Agarwal coined this to warn about missing engineering practices.
machine-speed.enLongDesc: Machine speed: the velocity at which AI agents can introduce bugs, tech debt, and inconsistencies. Without proper guardrails (tests, type checks, reviews), this speed becomes a liability.

llm.enShortDesc: Large Language Model: a function from text to text, trained on a large corpus. The foundation of modern AI assistants.
llm.enLongDesc: An LLM is a neural network trained on massive text corpora to predict the next token. Modern LLMs (GPT-4, Claude, Gemini) have hundreds of billions of parameters and exhibit emergent capabilities like reasoning and code generation.

context-window.enShortDesc: The maximum amount of text an LLM can process at once. 2026 standard: 1M tokens (Claude Opus 4.6), 2M tokens (Gemini 2.5 Pro).
context-window.enLongDesc:
The context window is the maximum input length an LLM can attend to. Measured in tokens (~0.75 English words or ~1.5 Chinese characters per token).

2026 standard: Claude Opus 4.6 ships 1M, Gemini 2.5 Pro reaches 2M, GPT-4o default 128K.

subagent.enShortDesc: A child agent spawned by a parent agent, with its own context window. Used for context isolation and parallel work.
subagent.enLongDesc:
A subagent runs within a single session but has its own context window. The parent agent delegates subtasks to keep its own context clean.

Pattern popularized by Claude Code in 2025.

tool-use.enShortDesc: The primitive that turns LLMs into agents: invoking external functions/APIs based on natural language decisions.
tool-use.enLongDesc: Tool use (a.k.a. function calling) lets an LLM decide which external function to call, with what arguments, based on the user's intent. This is the foundation of all AI agents.

mcp.enShortDesc: Model Context Protocol: Anthropic's open standard for connecting AI tools to external data sources and services.
mcp.enLongDesc: MCP is an open protocol (Anthropic, 2024) for connecting LLM applications to external tools and data. Standardizes how AI agents discover and invoke tools across vendors.

mcp-server.enShortDesc: A server implementation of MCP that exposes tools, prompts, or resources to MCP-compatible clients like Claude Code.
mcp-server.enLongDesc: An MCP server provides tools, resources, or prompts to any MCP-compatible client. Written in TypeScript or Python, deployable anywhere.

rag.enShortDesc: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: retrieve relevant documents, then have the LLM generate an answer based on the retrieved context.
rag.enLongDesc:
RAG augments LLM outputs with retrieved knowledge from a vector database or search index, reducing hallucinations and improving factual accuracy.

Original paper: Lewis et al. 2020.

embedding.enShortDesc: A dense numerical vector representing text, used for semantic search and similarity comparisons.
embedding.enLongDesc: An embedding maps text into a high-dimensional vector space where semantically similar texts are close together. Foundation of vector search and modern RAG systems.

vector-database.enShortDesc: A database optimized for storing and querying high-dimensional embedding vectors (Pinecone, Weaviate, ChromaDB, Qdrant).
vector-database.enLongDesc: A vector database stores embeddings and supports similarity search (k-nearest neighbors) at scale. Examples: Pinecone, Weaviate, ChromaDB, Qdrant, Milvus, pgvector.

cosine-similarity.enShortDesc: Similarity metric for vectors: measures the angle between them, ignoring magnitude. Standard for embedding comparisons.
cosine-similarity.enLongDesc: Cosine similarity = (a · b) / (||a|| × ||b||). Returns -1 (opposite) to 1 (same direction). Ideal for normalized embeddings because it ignores magnitude.

chunking.enShortDesc: Splitting long documents into smaller pieces for embedding and retrieval. Strategy choice (size, overlap) significantly affects RAG quality.
chunking.enLongDesc: Chunking divides documents into processable pieces (typically 500-2000 tokens). Chunk size and overlap are the most underrated RAG parameters.

reranker.enShortDesc: A second-pass model that re-scores vector search candidates for higher accuracy. Typically slower but more precise than embedding similarity.
reranker.enLongDesc: A reranker (e.g., Cohere Rerank, cross-encoder) takes the top-K results from a vector search and re-scores them with a more expensive model. Typically +15-30% retrieval accuracy.

hyde.enShortDesc: Hypothetical Document Embeddings: generate a hypothetical answer, embed it, then search. Outperforms query embedding for short questions.
hyde.enLongDesc: HyDE (Gao et al. 2022) generates a hypothetical answer via LLM, embeds that, and uses it for vector search. The hypothesis is closer to real document space than the raw question.

graph-rag.enShortDesc: RAG augmented with a knowledge graph: extract entities, build relationships, then query via community detection. Better for cross-chunk relational queries.
graph-rag.enLongDesc: GraphRAG (Microsoft, 2024) augments traditional vector RAG with a knowledge graph built from extracted entities and relationships. Enables global queries across chunks.

prompt-caching.enShortDesc: Cache prompt prefix to avoid recomputing KV cache on every request. Cuts cost by up to 90% for repeated system prompts.
prompt-caching.enLongDesc: Prompt caching (Anthropic, OpenAI) lets you mark a portion of the prompt as cacheable. Subsequent requests with the same prefix reuse the KV cache, dramatically reducing latency and cost.

transformer.enShortDesc: The neural architecture underlying all modern LLMs. Introduced in 'Attention Is All You Need' (Vaswani et al. 2017).
transformer.enLongDesc: The Transformer architecture (Vaswani et al. 2017) uses self-attention to process sequences in parallel. Foundation of GPT, BERT, T5, and essentially all modern LLMs.

attention.enShortDesc: The mechanism that lets models weigh the relevance of different input tokens to each other. Foundation of the Transformer.
attention.enLongDesc: Attention computes a weighted sum of values, where weights come from query-key dot products. Scaled dot-product attention is the standard variant.

kv-cache.enShortDesc: Cache of key/value matrices from previous tokens during autoregressive generation. Reduces per-token computation from O(n²) to O(n).
kv-cache.enLongDesc: KV cache stores previously computed key and value matrices, avoiding redundant computation during text generation. Memory grows linearly with sequence length.

paged-attention.enShortDesc: vLLM's memory management: page KV cache like OS virtual memory. 2-4x throughput improvement.
paged-attention.enLongDesc: PagedAttention (Kwon et al. SOSP 2023) borrows OS virtual memory concepts to manage LLM KV cache in fixed-size pages, reducing fragmentation and improving throughput 2-4x.

speculative-decoding.enShortDesc: Use a small draft model to generate candidates, then a large model verifies in parallel. 2-3x speedup with same output quality.
speculative-decoding.enLongDesc: Speculative decoding (Leviathan et al. 2022) uses a small fast model to draft multiple tokens, then the large model verifies them all in one forward pass. Same outputs, 2-3x faster.

flash-attention.enShortDesc: IO-aware exact attention algorithm. 2-4x wall-clock speedup, 5-10x memory reduction. By Tri Dao.
flash-attention.enLongDesc: Flash Attention (Dao et al. NeurIPS 2022) computes exact attention via tiling and recomputation, avoiding the O(n²) memory of the standard attention matrix. HuggingFace supports it via attn_implementation="flash_attention_2".

mixture-of-experts.enShortDesc: Sparse model architecture: many 'experts' but only top-k activated per token. DeepSeek V3: 671B params, 37B active.
mixture-of-experts.enLongDesc: Mixture of Experts (MoE) uses a router to select the top-k experts per token, keeping total parameter count high while active parameters per forward pass low. Enables trillion-parameter models at inference cost of much smaller ones.

mamba.enShortDesc: State Space Model alternative to Transformers. Linear O(n) complexity instead of quadratic. Strong for long sequences.
mamba.enLongDesc: Mamba (Gu & Dao 2023) is a selective state space model with linear-time sequence modeling. Trades off against attention for tasks requiring precise retrieval. Often combined with attention in hybrid models (e.g., Jamba).

rope.enShortDesc: Rotary Position Embedding: encodes position by rotating query/key vectors. Better length extrapolation than absolute positions.
rope.enLongDesc: RoPE (Su et al. 2021) encodes positional information by rotating the query and key vectors. Naturally supports relative positions and length extrapolation. Used in LLaMA, Mistral, many others.

alibi.enShortDesc: Attention with Linear Biases: a simple parameter-free positional encoding with strong length extrapolation.
alibi.enLongDesc: ALiBi (Press et al. 2022) adds a linear distance-based bias to attention scores instead of using learned positional embeddings. No extra parameters, strong length extrapolation.

router-gating.enShortDesc: A network that routes inputs to specific experts (in MoE) or to the most cost-effective model (multi-model systems).
router-gating.enLongDesc: Router/Gating networks decide which expert to use per token (MoE) or which LLM to query (FrugalGPT, RouteLLM). The routing function itself can be learned or rule-based.

encoder-decoder.enShortDesc: Transformer architecture with separate encoder and decoder. Used in T5, BART. Decoder-only is preferred for most LLMs.
encoder-decoder.enLongDesc: The encoder-decoder Transformer has two stacks: the encoder processes the input, the decoder generates output conditioned on the encoded input. Suited for translation and structured tasks.

structured-outputs.enShortDesc: Force the LLM to output JSON matching a specific schema. OpenAI's strict mode guarantees 100% schema compliance.
structured-outputs.enLongDesc: Structured outputs (OpenAI 2024, others) constrain the LLM to emit tokens matching a JSON schema. No retries needed; 100% schema-compliant. Use Pydantic or similar for type safety.

function-calling.enShortDesc: LLM decides which external function to call with what arguments. The primitive that turns LLMs into agents.
function-calling.enLongDesc: Function calling (a.k.a. tool use) lets the LLM emit structured calls to external functions. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google all support it via JSON schema definitions.

sampling.enShortDesc: Strategies for picking tokens from the LLM's probability distribution: greedy, top-k, top-p, temperature.
sampling.enLongDesc: Sampling controls randomness in token generation. Greedy (deterministic), top-k (limit to top K), top-p / nucleus (cumulative probability), and temperature (logit scaling) are the main strategies.

constrained-decoding.enShortDesc: Force LLM output to match a schema at the token level. Tools: Outlines, Guidance, JSONformer.
constrained-decoding.enLongDesc: Constrained decoding uses finite-state machines or context-free grammars to mask invalid tokens during generation. 100% guaranteed valid output, no retries.

quantization.enShortDesc: Reduce model precision (FP32 → FP16 → INT8 → INT4) to save memory and speed up inference. 4-bit is the sweet spot.
quantization.enLongDesc: Quantization maps weights from higher precision (FP32) to lower (INT4), reducing memory 4-8x with minimal accuracy loss. Methods: GPTQ, AWQ, bitsandbytes, SmoothQuant.

awq.enShortDesc: Activation-aware Weight Quantization: 4-bit quantization that preserves salient weights in higher precision. Quality-leading.
awq.enLongDesc: AWQ (Lin et al. 2023) protects the 1% most salient weights in FP16 and quantizes the rest to 4-bit. Better quality than GPTQ at the same bit width.

gptq.enShortDesc: GPT-style post-training quantization: layer-wise, second-order optimization. The first widely-used 4-bit method.
gptq.enLongDesc: GPTQ (Frantar et al. 2022) quantizes one layer at a time using second-order error compensation. Requires a small calibration set. Standard 4-bit method.

fine-tuning.enShortDesc: Adapting a pre-trained model to a specific task by continuing training on task-specific data.
fine-tuning.enLongDesc: Fine-tuning continues training a pre-trained model on task-specific data. Modern variants (LoRA, QLoRA) only train a small subset of parameters to save compute.

lora.enShortDesc: Low-Rank Adaptation: train 0.1% of parameters, retain 95%+ quality. The dominant efficient fine-tuning method.
lora.enLongDesc: LoRA (Hu et al. 2021) freezes pre-trained weights and adds a low-rank decomposition (A × B) that learns the task. Trains 0.1-1% of parameters, retains near-full quality.

qlora.enShortDesc: 4-bit quantized base + LoRA adapter. Trains a 65B model on a single 48GB GPU with no quality loss.
qlora.enLongDesc: QLoRA (Dettmers et al. 2023) combines 4-bit quantization of the base model with LoRA adapters in bf16. Enables fine-tuning of large models on consumer GPUs.

peft.enShortDesc: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: a unified library for LoRA, prefix tuning, prompt tuning, IA^3, and more.
peft.enLongDesc: PEFT (HuggingFace library) provides unified implementations of parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods. Train <1% of params, retain most quality.

distillation.enShortDesc: Train a small model to mimic a larger one's outputs. DistilBERT retains 97% of BERT quality at 60% size.
distillation.enLongDesc: Knowledge distillation trains a small (student) model to match the soft probability distribution of a larger (teacher) model. The student learns the teacher's 'dark knowledge' beyond hard labels.

frontier-model.enShortDesc: The most capable AI system at a given time. 2026 frontier: Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek V3.
frontier-model.enLongDesc: A frontier model is the most capable AI system available. 2026 frontier list: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context), GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro (2M context), DeepSeek V3, Llama 4.

code-model.enShortDesc: LLM specialized for code generation. Leaderboard: Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5-Codex, Qwen2.5-Coder.
code-model.enLongDesc: A code model is an LLM trained or fine-tuned specifically on code. Excels at fill-in-middle, multi-language understanding, and repository-level context (SWE-bench).

rlhf.enShortDesc: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: 3-stage training (SFT → Reward Model → PPO). The original alignment method.
rlhf.enLongDesc: RLHF (Ouyang et al. 2022) aligns LLMs to human preferences via: (1) supervised fine-tuning, (2) training a reward model on human preference rankings, (3) PPO reinforcement learning with the reward model.

dpo.enShortDesc: Direct Preference Optimization: replaces RLHF with a simple classification loss. No reward model needed.
dpo.enLongDesc: DPO (Rafailov et al. 2023) optimizes the LLM directly on preference pairs (chosen, rejected) using a simple cross-entropy loss. No reward model, more stable than RLHF.

rlaif.enShortDesc: RL from AI Feedback: use AI to label preferences, scaling RLHF without humans. Constitutional AI's foundation.
rlaif.enLongDesc: RLAIF (Lee et al. 2023, Anthropic Constitutional AI) replaces human preference labeling with AI-generated preferences based on a set of principles. Scalable, consistent.

hallucination.enShortDesc: When an LLM confidently states false information. The #1 reliability problem with LLMs.
hallucination.enLongDesc: A hallucination occurs when an LLM generates plausible but factually incorrect text, including invented citations, URLs, APIs, or facts. Mitigation: grounding via RAG, citations, and explicit uncertainty.

mcp-tool-search.enShortDesc: Tool search across many MCP servers: store tool descriptions in a vector DB, recall top-k on demand. Saves 85% tokens.
mcp-tool-search.enLongDesc: MCP tool search (Anthropic, 2025) avoids loading all tool descriptions into context. Indexes them in a vector DB and recalls only the top-k relevant per query.

channel.enShortDesc: In MCP, a typed conduit for sending messages between client, server, and the LLM (e.g., stdin/stdout, HTTP, WebSocket).
channel.enLongDesc: MCP channels define the transport between MCP components: stdio (local process), HTTP+SSE, or WebSocket. Channels are typed for safety.

connector.enShortDesc: In MCP, a plugin that bridges external services (databases, APIs) to the protocol. Connects data sources to LLMs.
connector.enLongDesc: MCP connectors are server-side adapters that expose external systems (Slack, GitHub, Postgres, etc.) as MCP resources/tools to any compliant client.

system-prompt.enShortDesc: The instruction sent to the LLM before any user message. Sets behavior, persona, and constraints.
system-prompt.enLongDesc: The system prompt (a.k.a. system message) is the highest-priority instruction sent to the LLM. Sets persona, constraints, output format. Cached by prompt caching for cost savings.

tokens.enShortDesc: The atomic unit LLMs process. ~0.75 English words or ~1.5 Chinese characters per token. Determines API pricing and context length.
tokens.enLongDesc: Tokens are the atomic units of LLM input/output. Text is split into tokens via BPE or WordPiece. ~0.75 English words per token, ~1.5 Chinese characters. Pricing and context limits are measured in tokens.

agent-loop.enShortDesc: The iterative cycle: gather context → take action → verify → repeat. The core pattern of all AI agents.
agent-loop.enLongDesc: The agent loop is the fundamental iteration pattern of AI agents: gather context, plan action, execute, observe result, verify, repeat until done or fail.

agent-teams.enShortDesc: Multiple AI agents collaborating in parallel, each with its own context window, sharing a task list (Claude Code Agent Teams, 2025).
agent-teams.enLongDesc: Agent teams (Claude Code 2025+) coordinate multiple agents in parallel: each has its own context window, they share a task list, and synchronize via worktrees.

orpo.enShortDesc: Odds Ratio Preference Optimization: combines SFT and DPO in one step. No reference model needed.
orpo.enLongDesc: ORPO (Hong et al. 2024) folds supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization into a single objective using odds ratio. No reference model, simpler pipeline than DPO.

ipo.enShortDesc: Identity Preference Optimization: fixes DPO's overfitting by using an identity instead of a log-sigmoid.
ipo.enLongDesc: IPO (Azar et al. 2023) replaces DPO's log-sigmoid with an identity loss, preventing the model from overfitting to preference data and producing deterministic outputs.

computer-use.enShortDesc: Anthropic's capability for Claude to control a computer: screenshot, mouse, keyboard. Released Oct 2024 for Sonnet 3.5.
computer-use.enLongDesc: Computer use (Anthropic, 2024-10) gives Claude access to screenshot, mouse, and keyboard tools, allowing it to operate desktop GUIs as a human would. Use cases: UI automation testing, form filling, cross-app workflows.

browser-use.enShortDesc: AI agent capability to control a web browser. Anthropic Claude for Chrome, browser-use open source library, OpenAI Operator.
browser-use.enLongDesc: Browser use lets AI agents automate web browsers via DOM, screenshots, or accessibility APIs. Examples: Claude for Chrome, the browser-use Python library, OpenAI Operator.

sdd.enShortDesc: Spec-Driven Development: using spec.md as a shared contract between humans, AI, tests, and reviewers.
sdd.enLongDesc:
SDD treats spec.md as the single source of truth. The spec is the contract between human intent, AI output, automated tests, and code review.

GitHub Spec Kit is the canonical toolchain (Specify / Plan / Tasks phases).

spec-md.enShortDesc: Using spec.md as the single source of truth (Single Source of Truth). Drives SDD workflows.
spec-md.enLongDesc: A spec.md file captures user stories, acceptance criteria, non-goals, and technical constraints in one place. Both humans and AI agents reference it as the contract.

context-engineering.enShortDesc: The engineering discipline of managing everything that enters the LLM's context window: instructions, tools, history, files.
context-engineering.enLongDesc:
Context engineering (Anthropic) is the discipline of curating what goes into the context window: system prompt, retrieved documents, tool definitions, conversation history, and file contents.

Related to but broader than prompt engineering.

plan-verify-build.enShortDesc: The core agent loop: plan, verify, build. The minimal viable workflow for AI coding.
plan-verify-build.enLongDesc: The Plan-Verify-Build loop: agent plans a step, the mechanical verification pipeline (compiler, tests, linter) validates, the agent builds. Repeat.

iterative-refinement.enShortDesc: Progressively improving output through multiple rounds of prompt adjustments. Each iteration gets closer to the goal.
iterative-refinement.enLongDesc: Iterative refinement: the model rarely produces the best output on the first try. Each round of feedback (more constraints, examples, edge cases) makes it sharper.

acceptance-criteria.enShortDesc: Pre-agreed, machine-verifiable 'definition of done'. Determines when vibe coding stops.
acceptance-criteria.enLongDesc:
Acceptance criteria are the machine-checkable conditions that define 'done'. Without them, vibe coding has no stopping rule.

Typically bullet-list checkboxes tied to tests or type checks.

tdd-ai.enShortDesc: Write the test first, then let the AI write the implementation. Simon Willison's recommended pattern for coding agents.
tdd-ai.enLongDesc: TDD with AI: invert the usual flow. Write a failing test (which serves as the spec), then prompt the AI to make it pass. The test is the contract.

claude-md.enShortDesc: Claude Code's project-level persistent instruction file. Auto-loaded at every session start.
claude-md.enLongDesc: CLAUDE.md is a markdown file in your project root (or ~/.claude/) that Claude Code reads at the start of every session. Persistent project conventions.

auto-memory.enShortDesc: Claude Code's self-written notes based on user corrections and preferences. Survives across git rebases.
auto-memory.enLongDesc: Auto memory: Claude Code learns from your corrections and writes notes that persist across sessions. Saved in ~/.claude/memory/.

compaction.enShortDesc: Auto-summarize the conversation when approaching the context window limit. Preserves context while freeing tokens.
compaction.enLongDesc: Compaction: when the conversation approaches the context window, summarize the older parts to make room. CLAUDE.md instructions survive compaction.

checkpoint.enShortDesc: File snapshot at each prompt. Roll back to any checkpoint via Esc Esc or /rewind.
checkpoint.enLongDesc: A checkpoint is a snapshot of the workspace state at a given prompt. Allows rewinding to any previous state without losing progress.

permission-mode.enShortDesc: Claude Code's base approval behavior. Cycle modes via Shift+Tab in the CLI.
permission-mode.enLongDesc: Permission mode controls which tool calls Claude Code can make without confirmation. Three modes: default (prompt for risky), acceptEdits, bypassPermissions.

auto-mode.enShortDesc: Background classifier that reviews operations. Doesn't see tool results, so immune to prompt injection.
auto-mode.enLongDesc: Auto mode: a background safety classifier approves or rejects agent actions. Crucially, it never sees tool results, so injected instructions cannot trick it.

bare-mode.enShortDesc: Launch Claude Code with --bare: no hooks, skills, or custom commands. Pure vanilla Claude Code.
bare-mode.enLongDesc: Bare mode: Claude Code started with --bare flag. Skips hooks, custom commands, and skills. Useful for debugging or CI consistency.

extended-thinking.enShortDesc: Claude's visible step-by-step reasoning before responding. Tunable via effort level.
extended-thinking.enLongDesc: Extended thinking: Claude performs chain-of-thought reasoning visible to the user before answering. Configurable via the thinking parameter and effort level.

effort-level.enShortDesc: Token budget for Claude's adaptive reasoning. Higher = deeper but slower.
effort-level.enLongDesc: Effort level controls how much compute Claude spends on extended thinking. Low for simple tasks, high for hard ones. Tunable per request.

output-style.enShortDesc: Modify Claude's system prompt to change response behavior, tone, or format.
output-style.enLongDesc: An output style (Claude Code) adjusts the system prompt to shape how Claude responds: explanatory, concise, structured, or default.

hooks.enShortDesc: Handlers (shell/HTTP) that auto-execute at specific points in the Claude Code lifecycle.
hooks.enLongDesc: Hooks are user-defined scripts triggered at events like PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, etc. Used for guardrails, logging, or automation.

bundled-skills.enShortDesc: Claude Code's built-in prompt-based playbooks like /batch /loop /init. Auto-available.
bundled-skills.enLongDesc: Bundled skills are Claude Code's built-in playbooks: pre-configured prompts for common tasks (e.g., /batch for batch operations, /loop for retries).

commands.enShortDesc: Reusable instructions invoked via /name. Built-in plus user-defined.
commands.enLongDesc: Commands are reusable prompts triggered by typing /name. Claude Code has built-in commands; users can add custom ones in .claude/commands/.

cursor.enShortDesc: AI-first IDE based on a VS Code fork. Flagship vibe coding tool.
cursor.enLongDesc: Cursor is an AI-first IDE built on a VS Code fork. Features Tab autocomplete, Chat (@code), Composer (multi-file agent), and Agent Mode. Supports Claude, GPT, Gemini.

cursor-composer.enShortDesc: Cursor's multi-file edit + agent orchestration feature. The flagship vibe coding workflow.
cursor-composer.enLongDesc: Composer is Cursor's agent for multi-file edits: reads relevant files, generates unified diffs across many files, shows a plan for review, then applies in one shot.

claude-code.enShortDesc: Anthropic's CLI agent for the terminal. Recommended by Karpathy.
claude-code.enLongDesc: Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal-based coding agent. Uses Claude models with tool use (Read, Edit, Bash), subagents, checkpoints, hooks, and CLAUDE.md for persistence.

windsurf.enShortDesc: Codeium's AI IDE, direct competitor to Cursor.
windsurf.enLongDesc: Windsurf is Codeium's AI-native IDE. Features Cascade (agent flow), Supercomplete (inline suggestions), and Flow for multi-file edits.

copilot.enShortDesc: The earliest mainstream AI coding assistant (2021). Highest adoption rate.
copilot.enLongDesc: GitHub Copilot (2021) pioneered AI code completion. Inline suggestions + chat (Copilot Chat). Backed by OpenAI Codex / GPT models.

aider.enShortDesc: AI pair programmer in the terminal. Open source. Multi-LLM backend.
aider.enLongDesc: Aider is a terminal-based AI pair programming tool. Reads git-tracked files, edits, and auto-commits. Supports many LLM backends.

replit-agent.enShortDesc: Agent built into Replit's cloud IDE. In July 2025, it deleted a user's production database during a code execution.
replit-agent.enLongDesc: Replit Agent is the agent built into Replit's cloud IDE. Builds and deploys full-stack apps from natural language. Has had notable production incidents.

lovable.enShortDesc: Swedish startup focused on frontend vibe coding. Had a PII leak incident in May 2025.
lovable.enLongDesc: Lovable is a frontend vibe coding platform. Generates React + Tailwind from prompts, deploys to a custom domain. Target: non-developers building SaaS frontends.

codeium.enShortDesc: Free AI code completion tool. Parent company of Windsurf.
codeium.enLongDesc: Codeium provides free AI code completion. Acquired by / merged with Windsurf. Supports many languages and IDEs.

tabnine.enShortDesc: Early AI code completion tool, focused on on-prem deployment and privacy.
tabnine.enLongDesc: Tabnine offers AI code completion with optional on-prem model deployment for code privacy. Enterprise-friendly.

cline.enShortDesc: VS Code extension that turns the IDE into an agent workbench.
cline.enLongDesc: Cline (formerly Claude Dev) is a VS Code extension that lets Claude autonomously edit files, run commands, and use a browser. Open source.

devin.enShortDesc: Cognition AI's 'first AI software engineer' — an autonomous agent.
devin.enLongDesc: Devin is Cognition AI's autonomous coding agent. Receives tickets, spins up a sandbox, clones the repo, codes, tests, and submits PRs. Marketed as the first AI engineer.

v0.enShortDesc: Vercel's frontend vibe coding platform. Prompt to React component.
v0.enLongDesc: v0 (Vercel) generates React + Tailwind + shadcn/ui components from natural language prompts. Designed for copy-paste into your codebase.

coderabbit.enShortDesc: AI code review agent for GitHub PRs. Research shows it increases security vulnerabilities.
coderabbit.enLongDesc: CodeRabbit is an AI PR reviewer that comments on GitHub pull requests. Research (2025) found AI co-authored code had 2.74x more security vulnerabilities.

veracode.enShortDesc: Security scanning platform. Research shows LLM-generated code security hasn't improved over 3 years.
veracode.enLongDesc: Veracode is an application security testing platform. Their 2025 report found LLM-generated code security has not improved in 3 years; larger models aren't more secure than smaller ones.

spec-kit.enShortDesc: GitHub's open-source SDD toolchain. Specify / Plan / Tasks three phases.
spec-kit.enLongDesc: GitHub Spec Kit is an open-source toolchain for Spec-Driven Development. Three phases: specify (generate spec.md), plan (architecture), tasks (checklist).

gemini-cli.enShortDesc: Google's CLI agent, similar to Claude Code.
gemini-cli.enLongDesc: Gemini CLI is Google's terminal-based coding agent powered by Gemini 2.5 Pro. Open source. Supports long contexts (1M+).

codex-cli.enLongDesc: Codex CLI is OpenAI's terminal agent. Uses GPT-5-Codex. Released April 2025 as part of OpenAI's coding tooling.

coding-agents.enShortDesc: Simon Willison's term: tools that iteratively code, test, and modify until the goal is met.
coding-agents.enLongDesc: Coding agents (Willison) are AI tools that iteratively plan, code, test, and refine until they reach a goal. Distinct from one-shot completions.

antigravity.enLongDesc: Antigravity is Google's AI-native IDE released in 2025. Built on VS Code. Competes with Cursor and Windsurf.

langchain.enShortDesc: LLM application orchestration framework. 600+ integrations, LangGraph for stateful agents.
langchain.enLongDesc: LangChain orchestrates LLM workflows with 600+ integrations. LCEL for chain composition; LangGraph for stateful multi-agent systems.

llamaindex.enShortDesc: Focused on RAG pipelines. Node-based document model and query engines.
llamaindex.enLongDesc: LlamaIndex is a data framework for LLM applications, with first-class RAG support. Indexes documents as nodes, exposes query engines and agents.

dspy.enShortDesc: Stanford's LLM program optimization framework. Prompts as compilable code.
dspy.enLongDesc: DSPy (Stanford NLP) treats prompts as code: you write signatures and modules, then optimizers (BootstrapFewShot, MIPRO) compile them against your training data.

huggingface.enShortDesc: Open-source ML model and dataset platform. Home of the Transformers library.
huggingface.enLongDesc: Hugging Face hosts models, datasets, and Spaces. The Transformers library is the de facto standard for open LLM inference and fine-tuning.

mcp-tool-server.enShortDesc: Hundreds of MCP servers provide integrations for Slack, Jira, databases, browsers, etc.
mcp-tool-server.enLongDesc: Public MCP servers provide tools for common services: filesystem, GitHub, Slack, Postgres, Playwright, etc. Search the MCP registry or build your own.

orchids.enShortDesc: One of several vibe coding platforms.
orchids.enLongDesc: Orchids is a vibe coding platform for building apps from natural language prompts.

openclaw.enShortDesc: AI agent system including 'Pi coding harness'. Created by Mario Zechner and others.
openclaw.enLongDesc: OpenClaw is an open-source AI agent framework that includes the 'Pi coding harness'. Inspired by Anthropic's Claude Code.

superwhisper.enShortDesc: Speech-to-text tool that lets users talk to LLMs via voice.
superwhisper.enLongDesc: SuperWhisper is a voice-to-text tool optimized for code and technical conversations. Enables hands-free prompting of LLMs.
